# How to Prepare Your Home Before a Cleaner Arrives (Cape Town Guide)

Good preparation does not mean **pre-cleaning** your home out of embarrassment. It means removing **friction** so a professional can spend minutes on **soil and hygiene**, not on guessing which sink is yours, where to park, or whether the dog is friendly.

This guide sits in **Cluster 2 — booking confidence and expectations**. It supports—but does not replace—the decision, urgency, scope, timing, and cadence layers linked below. If you need **what is in the checklist**, read [**what’s included in a deep clean**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/whats-included-in-deep-cleaning-cape-town). If you need **how long visits run**, read [**how long house cleaning takes**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/how-long-does-house-cleaning-take-cape-town). If you are choosing **tier**, start with [**deep vs standard—which to book**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/deep-vs-standard-cleaning-which-to-book-cape-town).

Whether you live in a compact **Sea Point** apartment, a busy **Claremont** family home, a wind-exposed **Constantia** house, a **Century City** weekday rhythm, or a **Green Point** Airbnb with tight turnovers—**access + clarity** beat a last-minute panic tidy.

---

## Quick answer: do you need to clean before a cleaner arrives?

**No**—you do not need to “deep clean before the deep clean.” **Tidying** (clearing surfaces, dishes out of the sink, toys off the floor) is different from **cleaning** (sanitising, degreasing, dusting, mopping). Give cleaners **workflow**: clear paths, honest priorities, and parking or estate notes so booked time becomes **cleaning time**, not detective work.

---

## What you should do before professional cleaners arrive

- **Declutter surfaces** you want wiped—kitchen islands, bathroom vanities, coffee tables. Put paperwork and small items in drawers or baskets.
- **Secure valuables** in a locked room or safe—reduces anxiety for everyone without implying mistrust.
- **Pets**: a closed room, crate, or arranged outing keeps animals calm and keeps teams efficient.
- **Parking and kerb rules**: bay numbers, disc requirements, and “no stopping” windows—especially near **Sea Point** and **Green Point** strips.
- **Building access**: buzzer codes, lift fobs, estate gate colours, contractor decals, and who to call if intercom fails—**security estates** in **Claremont** and **Constantia** eat minutes when notes are vague.
- **Load-shedding**: if your block is dark during the slot, say how cleaners should enter and whether stairs are lit.
- **Two-line priorities**: “Focus kitchen + main bath; skip spare room today.” That pairs with honest scope in booking—not surprise scope at the door.

---

## What you do **not** need to do

- You do **not** need to **scrub** ovens or grout “so the cleaner does not judge you.”
- You do **not** need to **hide normal life**—lived-in homes are expected.
- You do **not** need to buy **premium products**; professional visits include supplies unless your booking says otherwise.
- You do **not** need to **re-explain** everything in person if you already wrote clear notes—especially helpful for recurring visits.

Relaxing here usually improves outcomes: calmer handovers, clearer priorities, fewer rushed corners.

---

## How preparation improves cleaning results

When surfaces are reachable and access is smooth, crews spend more minutes on **high-touch zones**—kitchens and bathrooms—where hygiene scores matter most. Less shuffle means **better sinks, better baths**, and fewer delays that squeeze the **next** client on the route. That is the same practical logic behind [**timing estimates**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/how-long-does-house-cleaning-take-cape-town): clutter steals clock.

---

## Apartment vs house preparation in Cape Town

**Apartments** (Atlantic Seaboard, CBD-adjacent, **Green Point**): lifts, intercoms, visitor parking discs, and narrow kerbs are the usual friction. A photo of your parking bay in booking notes beats a long voice note.

**Houses** (**Claremont**, **Constantia**, **Century City** suburbs): long driveways, side gates, dogs in gardens, and “park behind the grey Corolla” instructions matter. Mention alarm behaviour if cleaners disarm.

Same rule for both: **accurate address + access** is part of preparation.

---

## Preparing for same-day cleaning

If you are booking **today**, preparation matters more because routing has less slack. Read [**same-day cleaning in Cape Town**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/same-day-cleaning-cape-town): same-day is **availability**, not unlimited scope. Tight notes and realistic room counts prevent “calendar yes, on-site squeeze.”

---

## What helps cleaners work faster?

- Clear sinks (dishes rinsed or stacked neatly)
- Accessible bathrooms (towels hung, laundry off the floor)
- Floors walkable without tripping hazards
- **Accurate bedroom and bathroom counts** in checkout—matches [**which tier to book**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/deep-vs-standard-cleaning-which-to-book-cape-town) honesty
- Laundry baskets out of the wet-room path
- Bins emptied if you want interior bin work in scope

---

## Common mistakes before a cleaning appointment

- **Underestimating clutter** and expecting “magic reset” in the same booked window
- **Vague access** (“call me”) when you will be in meetings
- **Changing priorities at the door** instead of updating booking notes
- **Forgetting parking** and losing 10 minutes on the kerb
- **Assuming** add-ons without ticking them—scope lives in [**what’s included**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/whats-included-in-deep-cleaning-cape-town) + your selections

---

## How to get the best results from professional cleaning

- **Communicate once, clearly**—written beats improvised.
- **Match scope to soil truth**—[**deep vs standard**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/deep-vs-standard-cleaning-which-to-book-cape-town).
- **Use recurring rhythm** when the home needs predictability—[**once-off vs recurring**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/once-off-vs-recurring-cleaning-cape-town).
- **Book standard or deep** with line-item clarity: [**standard cleaning Cape Town**](https://shalean.co.za/services/standard-cleaning-cape-town) · [**deep cleaning Cape Town**](https://shalean.co.za/services/deep-cleaning-cape-town)

### Mid-article CTA

Prepared the basics? Open [**standard**](https://shalean.co.za/services/standard-cleaning-cape-town) or [**deep**](https://shalean.co.za/services/deep-cleaning-cape-town), enter rooms and tier honestly, then confirm—your total stays transparent before you pay.

---

## Frequently asked questions

### Should I tidy before cleaners arrive?

Yes—**tidy** surfaces and floors so cleaners can clean. You do not need to scrub; you need to remove obstacles and fragile clutter.

### What should I put away before cleaning?

Cash, jewellery, small electronics, and private paperwork. Clearing counters helps teams work without guessing what is “off limits.”

### Do cleaners bring their own supplies?

Usually yes for professional visits unless your booking states otherwise. Add allergy or product notes if needed.

### Should I stay home during cleaning?

Only if you want to—many clients provide access instructions instead. Whatever you choose, access must be reliable.

### How do I prepare pets for a cleaner visit?

Secure pets in a closed room or arrange an outing. Note behaviour (door dasher, anxious barker) in booking notes.

### Do I need to clean my bathroom before the cleaner cleans it?

No. A quick tidy (towels, laundry off the floor) helps; pre-scrubbing is not required.

### Will preparation change how long the visit takes?

Often yes—less clutter usually means more minutes on hygiene tasks. Heavy clutter can shorten effective cleaning time within the same booking window.

### What if I live in a security estate?

Add gate rules, visitor decals, intercom spelling, and parking bay numbers **before** the visit—estate friction is a Cape Town routine reality.

### How does this relate to same-day bookings?

Same-day has tighter routing—clear notes matter more. Read the [**same-day guide**](https://shalean.co.za/blog/same-day-cleaning-cape-town) and keep scope realistic.

---

---

## End CTA

Preparation builds **confidence**: you are not buying mystery labour—you are buying a clear visit with [**standard**](https://shalean.co.za/services/standard-cleaning-cape-town) or [**deep**](https://shalean.co.za/services/deep-cleaning-cape-town) scope you already thought through. When you are ready, book online and keep access notes and priorities current so the visit stays focused on hygiene and outcomes.
